change: AC-2: journal-only action counts (sent, waived, failed, interrupted, pending) always reported, attention[] always lists failed/blocked nodes and failed/interrupted actions. AC-4: without --with-tests no due/held-unverified keys and no unverified/held-unverified attention entries; with it due + held-unverified split pending by FR-NODE-251 AC-4. New AC-7: wave status --with-tests due/held-unverified counts equal wave actions. Bucket name held -> held-unverified.

AC-5: argument-free leaf reads the run's latest graph reference (latest redecompose line, else first line) and compares the digest against it. New AC-8: after a recorded redecompose (same or other path) no graph-digest-mismatch, hand edit without a journal line still reports it.
Rationale lines: AC-2 adds PRD-24, AC-5 adds PRD-21, new AC-7 (fills: PRD-10 / hole) and AC-8 (PRD-21, PRD-10).

AC-3: journal state per action with no scan (pending, sent, waived, interrupted, failed) for a node whose latest line is complete. AC-4: wave actions splits pending into due (scanned done) or held-unverified (scanned unverified), other journal states kept whatever the scanned state.
AC-1: without --waves the graph is found through the run's latest graph reference, as IR-CLI-113 AC-5.
AC-2: only a state computed with the scan decides whether a pending action is due or held-unverified (FR-NODE-251 AC-4, IR-CLI-113 AC-4).

AC-1: journal append refuses a graph on a line that is neither the first line nor a redecompose line. AC-2: redecompose line requires graph {path, digest} (same or other path), refused when missing or malformed; latest graph reference defined as latest redecompose line's graph, else first line's.
Statement names the graph reference on each redecompose line and the current graph version.
Rationale split into one line per AC, AC-2 adds PRD-10.
AC-3: new graph version over the same path or another path, redecompose line carries its graph {path, digest} (FR-NODE-250 AC-2).
AC-1: skills record the graph on the first line and each redecomposed version's graph on its redecompose line.
